papers.title_en: AtomTree: A Hierarchical Framework for State-Aware Embodied Instruction Following with LLMs
papers.authors: Haotian Zhai, Tianming Sha, Junnan Li
papers.evidence: 大模型分层状态感知任务规划，分解子目标与动作
papers.tldr: 交互环境中的具身指令跟随需要长程规划，现有LLM规划器一次性生成计划、依赖语言常识且仅在失败后更新，状态感知与鲁棒性不足。AtomTree用LLM增量构建子目标与动作树，依据当前符号状态逐步决定分解或输出可执行低层动作，并用轻量记忆复用历史结果。当动作停滞时触发分层回溯重规划，从最新状态重建子树。在ALFRED零样本评测中优于先前LLM规划器。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied instruction following in interactive environments requires agents to interpret natural language commands and complete long-horizon tasks. Existing planners either rely on large labeled trajectories, or use few-shot and zero-shot LLM prompting that produces a whole plan in a single serial reasoning process. These approaches depend on linguistic common sense, commit to a plan from the initial instruction, and only update after failures, which weakens robustness and state awareness. We present AtomTree, a hierarchical framework for state-aware task planning with LLMs. AtomTree incrementally builds a tree of subgoals and actions, where the LLM decides at each step, from the current symbolic state, whether to further decompose or to output a grounded low-level action. A lightweight memory module summarizes past outcomes for reuse in later decisions. When a low-level action stalls, AtomTree triggers hierarchical backtracking replanning to return to the parent node and regenerate the subtree plan from the latest state, preventing continued drift along an incorrect trajectory. In zero-shot evaluation on the ALFRED benchmark, AtomTree outperforms prior LLM-based planners. Project page: https://zhaihaotian.github.io/atomtree-website/.

papers.title_en: ESI: An Embodied Self-Improvement Flywheel for LLM-VLA Agents
papers.authors: Yundi Cai, Zihan Wang, Chenxi Han, Yi Cheng, Houde Liu, Zilei Wang
papers.evidence: LLM规划子任务并调用VLA技能接口执行
papers.tldr: LLM与VLA独立预训练虽互补，但直接连接常出现动作偏离子任务、纠错后回退状态等协同问题。ESI将模块化智能体作为后训练单元，利用环境交互反复优化LLM提示、共享技能接口与VLA参数并整体重部署，以协作过程提供语义与动作级监督。在10个RoboDojo任务上，无任务专用控制代码即达62.03分和49.41%成功率，超过GO-3 Nano Preview等混合智能体与代码方法。
papers.abstract_en: Independently pretrained language models and vision-language-action (VLA) policies provide complementary building blocks for embodied agents, but connecting them does not automatically produce coordinated behavior. The VLA may generate actions that diverge from the LLM's intended subtask and, upon regaining control after a correction, undo the promising state restored by the LLM. We introduce ESI (Embodied Self-Improvement), an automated flywheel that uses environmental interaction to align reasoning and action. ESI treats the modular agent as the unit of post-training, repeatedly refining the prompts that guide the LLM, the shared skill interface that expresses its intent, and the VLA parameters that realize that intent, then redeploying these components together. Our key insight is that collaboration itself can supply supervision for improving this interface. The LLM's subtask decisions provide semantic supervision for what the policy should execute, while its effective corrections and subsequent student continuations provide action-level supervision for recovery and handoff. The student also learns from its own effective execution, allowing locally useful experience to contribute even when the overall episode fails. On ten selected RoboDojo tasks, ESI achieves a mean Score of 62.03 and a mean success rate of 49.41% using an LLM-VLA agent without generating task-specific control code. On both metrics, it outperforms the published reference results of all hybrid embodied agents, including the Agent+WAM system GO-3 Nano Preview (47.27 Score and 36.60% success), as well as all compared code-based methods.

papers.title_en: Body and Soul: Decoupling Robotic Brain and Policy with RoboHarness-Zero
papers.authors: Yihao Shen, Yuxuan Chen, Xuantong Liu, Jun Gao, Weijian Luo, Tianyang Hu
papers.evidence: VLM外层框架包裹冻结VLA以串联多项技能
papers.tldr: 视觉语言动作（VLA）策略能执行单项技能，却难以完成需要组合多技能的长程任务。RoboHarness-Zero 用冻结 VLM 作为外层调度器，零样本规划目标并监控进度，仅在停滞时改写指令或调用通用运动原语代码，随后交还控制权给冻结 VLA。在 RoboCasa365 的 200 个场景中，冻结的 Xiaomi-Robotics-1 成功率从 57.5% 提升到 70.5%，并保留 90.4% 的原有成功。该框架无需任务准备、换策略只需薄适配层，可跨策略迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can execute individual skills but fail to complete tasks that require combining several of them. In our audit of Xiaomi-Robotics-1, an estimated 43\% of failures involve choosing the wrong target or losing track of task progress. Wrapping a frozen VLA in a vision-language model (VLM) harness is a natural remedy. Existing harnesses can gain substantially from task- and policy-specific preparation, raising the question of how much of that gain transfers to a new task or policy. An ideal harness should (i) need minimal preparation for a new task, (ii) need no redesign for a new policy, and (iii) preserve standalone capabilities the policy already has. To the best of our knowledge, our \ours{} is the first harness built this way. Its premise is that choosing targets and tracking progress are easy for a VLM such as GPT-6 without task preparation, while the frozen VLA already handles continuous, contact-rich motion. The frozen VLA therefore executes continuous control while the VLM plans zero-shot and monitors execution; when progress stalls or targets drift, the VLM first rephrases the instruction and, only as a fallback, executes short generated code over generic motion primitives before returning fine control to the VLA. The supervision rules stay fixed across policies, requiring only a thin interface adapter and an automatically profiled skill configuration per policy. On 200 RoboCasa365 scenes, \ours{} with GPT-6 Astra raises the success rate of frozen Xiaomi-Robotics-1 from \textbf{\color{blue}57.5\%} to \textbf{\color{blue}70.5\%} and preserves \textbf{\color{blue}90.4\%} of its standalone successes (104/115) while rescuing 37 of 85 failures. On a shared 50-scene subset, the same rules add 8 to 10 percentage points to each of four other frozen policies, while existing preparation-based harness systems often fail to transfer to a new policy.

papers.title_en: LLM-Guided Compositional Continual Learning for Robot Manipulation with Gated Low-Rank Experts
papers.authors: Nilay Kushawaha, Abdalla Swikir, Fares Abu-Dakka
papers.evidence: 冻结的本地大模型将指令分解为子任务并路由到技能专家
papers.tldr: 针对机器人持续学习新技能易遗忘、密集PNN旁路参数开销大的问题，提出LLM引导的组合式持续学习框架：每项技能对应PNN专家，并用带可学习父级门控的LoRA旁路复用旧知识。冻结本地LLM将长程自然语言指令分解并路由到专家，不足时按需新增专家。在12个MetaWorld任务及Sawyer到Panda再到UR5e的跨本体迁移中，少样本下任务成功率优于从头学习。真机实验验证了组合执行与专家编排能力。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose manipulation robots must acquire new skills over time without forgetting prior ones or retraining from scratch. We present a continual learning framework that represents each skill as a dedicated expert sub- network in a Progressive Neural Network (PNN). New tasks reuse prior knowledge through low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules on lateral connections controlled by learnable per-parent gates, enabling explicit attenuation of individual transfer paths while reducing the parameter cost of dense PNN laterals. For long-horizon deployment, a frozen local large language model decomposes natural-language instructions into sub-tasks, routes them to suitable experts, and requests a new expert only when the library is insufficient. Using a shared task-space action interface, we evaluate the framework on twelve MetaWorld tasks and in a Sawyer-to-Panda-to-UR5e cross-embodiment transfer experiment, showing improved task success relative to learning from scratch when demonstrations are limited. Real-robot manipulation experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework supports compositional execution and expert orchestration.

papers.title_en: Just-in-Time Skill Retrieval via Long-Horizon State Tracking
papers.authors: Xin Lin, Ziheng Wang, Zerui Chen, Jiayao Ma, Zhimin Wei, Bingshuai Liu, Buchao Zhan, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su
papers.evidence: 大模型智能体在执行过程中动态从技能库检索技能
papers.tldr: 长程任务中，LLM智能体若在执行前一次性固定技能集合，往往难以应对执行过程中由中间观察、执行结果和新约束触发的新需求。JitSkill提出即时技能检索，通过持续跟踪任务状态，将涌现需求与已积累进展关联，动态选择当前所需技能。它在三个智能体基准上提升了长程任务完成表现。该工作表明，状态感知的动态技能选择比静态预选更适合复杂长程执行。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external skill libraries to support complex task execution. However, determining which skills are needed remains challenging in long-horizon tasks. Existing methods typically select a fixed skill set before execution, implicitly assuming that a task's procedural requirements can be determined from its initial description. This assumption is restrictive for long-horizon interaction, where new requirements emerge from intermediate observations, execution outcomes, and newly revealed constraints. This motivates just-in-time skill retrieval, which dynamically selects skills as execution unfolds. Just-in-time skill retrieval is promising but challenging: the utility of a skill depends not only on the current context, but also on the evolving task state shaped by prior steps. To this end, we propose JitSkill, a state-grounded framework that addresses this challenge through continuous task-state tracking. By connecting emerging requirements with accumulated task progress, JitSkill provides procedural support throughout execution without treating each retrieval decision independently. Experiments across three agent benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness in improving long-horizon task completion. Our code is available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/JitSkill.git/.

papers.title_en: Think with Skills: Pseudocode Planning Before Execution for Advanced Reasoners
papers.authors: Boshen Zhou, Boxuan Yue, Xiang Li, Shanchao Yang
papers.evidence: 训练推理模型将技能描述转为伪代码计划并安排技能顺序
papers.tldr: 语言模型代理即使掌握专家编写的技能，也常因技能仅编码陈述性知识、缺少任务特定程序性知识而难以完成复杂任务。Think with Skills 先训练推理模型把相关技能描述转化为任务特定伪代码计划，显式表示操作、条件、中间结果与依赖，再据此执行。在 SkillsBench 上，任务成功率从35.0%提升至62.0%。这说明执行前将专家知识程序化，能为技能描述到代理行动提供结构化桥梁并显著改善技能使用。
papers.abstract_en: Language model agents often struggle with complex tasks even when equipped with expert-written skills. Such skills encode declarative knowledge, whereas successful execution requires procedural knowledge tailored to the task at hand. Natural language skills may leave conditions and dependencies implicit, and tasks involving multiple skills further require agents to coordinate intermediate results and execution order. We introduce Think with Skills, a method that trains reasoning models to turn relevant skill descriptions into task-specific pseudocode plans before execution. The pseudocode explicitly represents operations, conditions, intermediate results, and dependencies, providing a structured bridge from skill descriptions to agent actions. We construct training data that pairs tasks and skills with pseudocode plans and execution trajectories, use supervised fine tuning to initialize this behavior, and further optimize end-to-end task performance with Group Relative Policy Optimization. On SkillsBench, Think with Skills raises task success from 35.0% to 62.0%. These results show that proceduralizing expert knowledge before execution substantially improves skill use.

papers.title_en: RoboCoEvo: Expanding Robot Capabilities through Agent-Policy Co-Evolution
papers.authors: Ran Qi, Yixin Xiao, Dawei Wang, Zhiyuan Li, Jinbang Huang, Xuan Zhao, Yintao Ma, Yangzheng Wu, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang
papers.evidence: 基于MLLM的智能体与机器人基础模型协同进化以扩展机器人能力
papers.tldr: 现有MLLM智能体与机器人基础模型多各自改进、协同增益受限，RoboCoEvo提出失败引导的智能体-策略协同进化框架。它用代码即策略让智能体生成并迭代故障检测与恢复程序，再把纠正行为后训练进VLA端到端策略，并由新故障分布反向指导程序修订。在BEHAVIOR-1K、RoboCasa和RoboTwin上，多轮协同进化持续提升自主VLA任务表现。该工作把智能体可复用知识与机器人策略参数学习耦合起来，为扩展机器人能力提供闭环路径。
papers.abstract_en: Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models has attracted increasing attention as a means of enhancing robotic capabilities. However, the improvement of such integrated systems remains largely decoupled across their agent and model components, with advances in one component not necessarily benefiting the other, substantially limiting the capabilities of the combined system. As both MLLMs and robotic foundation models become increasingly capable, fully realizing their combined potential calls for co-evolution, an iterative process in which improvements in agents and robotic foundation models reinforce one another. We propose RoboCoEvo, a failure-guided co-evolution framework that couples the refinement of the agent's explicit and reusable executable knowledge with parameter learning in robotic foundation models, such as vision-language-action (VLA) models. Through a code-as-policy formulation, the agent develops and refines executable failure-detection and recovery programs, generating targeted corrective experience. Post-training consolidates the resulting corrective behaviors into the robotic model's end-to-end policy, improving autonomous task execution. Changes in the updated policy's failure distribution, in turn, guide subsequent revisions to the agent's programs. Experiments on BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin demonstrate sustained improvements in autonomous VLA task performance across successive co-evolution rounds.

papers.title_en: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Zilang Cen, Chao Tang, Fangcheng Liu, Weishi Mi, Wei Hao, JiaYu Xu, Dehao Huang, Yehui Tang, Xiaohui Cui, Tingguang Li, Xiaoyuan Zhang
papers.evidence: 高层推理智能体监控子任务进展并协调低层策略完成长时程执行
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作若频繁调用大模型，会带来高延迟与高 token 成本，且难以判断何时介入及修复执行还是计划。RoC 用在线任务状态监控器融合时序视觉与有序交互记忆，估计子任务进度并预测后继，触发事件驱动复核，协同修复执行与修订计划。RMBench 上成功率较最强智能体基线提升 24.0 个百分点、token 降 65.3%，并超最强策略基线 15.1 个百分点。真实世界三项长程任务验证其高效干预与协同恢复能力。
papers.abstract_en: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

papers.title_en: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding
papers.authors: Buzhao Liu, Jianing Ye, Xiu Yuan, Yangtong Feng, Chengsong Huang, Tyler Dinh, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, Ning Zhang, Chongjie Zhang
papers.evidence: 大模型智能体在多层级物理理解下搜索模块化机器人程序
papers.tldr: LLM 智能体在机器人操作中可用 Code-as-Policy 搜索程序，但缺乏对物体可供性、场景几何与交互成败原因的物理理解，仅靠执行反馈难以纠错。RoboAuto 从物体、场景、交互三个层级显式组织物理理解：分层知识库结合可执行技能与物体知识，场景接地将知识对齐当前环境，多阶段规划配合自设实验验证各阶段物理效果并主动检验竞争假设。在五个基准族上取得领先，LIBERO-PRO 短程任务成功率 89.1%，长程与 LIBERO-Plus 上平均成功率超 ASPIRE 两倍。
papers.abstract_en: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. In robotic manipulation, Code-as-Policy lets these agents search over modular and editable robot programs. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Existing methods rely mainly on execution feedback for program refinement, often leaving these physical questions unresolved. We introduce RoboAuto, a framework for robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels through three components. First, a hierarchical knowledge base combines executable skills with object-centric knowledge of affordances, spatial relations, and action effects, learned from embodied data and online task solving. Second, scene grounding connects this knowledge to the current environment by identifying relevant objects and resolving action-critical quantities. Third, multi-stage planning with self-designed experiments checks whether each stage produces its expected physical effects and actively tests competing hypotheses to resolve physical uncertainties. RoboAuto achieves superior performance across five benchmark families, attaining an 89.1% success rate on short-horizon LIBERO-PRO tasks and more than twice the mean success rate of ASPIRE on LIBERO-PRO Long and LIBERO-Plus. It also outperforms ASPIRE and $π_{0.5}$ on three challenging long-horizon real-robot tasks requiring precise manipulation. We further show that the knowledge base transfers across simulators and embodiments, and that program search performance scales with its size. Project page: https://roboauto-ai.github.io/

papers.title_en: Learning from Physical Experience:Context-Space Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Yihan Zeng, Yisu Li, Kaixin Huang, Marc WuDunn, Amelia Kovacs, Mikael Harseno, Kimmy Lin, Porter Hunley, Fred Shentu, Philipp Wu, Zhongyu Li, Zike Yan
papers.evidence: 通用推理大模型作为操作策略并承担任务级规划
papers.tldr: 通用多模态基础模型推理强，但转化为机器人操作动作仍困难。LEXP通过任务规划与经验模块，将执行证据提炼为带适用条件的经验，并复用生成上下文反馈，且不更新模型权重与动作接口。在12个真实操作任务中成功23/36，优于仅记忆19/36与原始Astra 2/36；消融显示规划与经验均关键。该工作表明上下文空间适应可把物理交互转化为可复用操作指导。
papers.abstract_en: Recent multimodal foundation models exhibit strong perception, reasoning, and in-context learning capabilities, but translating these capabilities into physical action remains challenging. Through real-world experiments across diverse manipulation tasks, we find that ChatGPT-6-Astra, a state-of-the-art general-purpose reasoner, can serve as a physically actionable, context-responsive manipulation policy, demonstrating effective fine manipulation and spatial reasoning. Building on these findings, we introduce LEXP, a harness for learning from physical experience through context-space adaptation. LEXP combines task-level planning with an experience module that interprets execution evidence, extracts and retains lessons with applicability conditions, and reuses relevant lessons to generate contextual feedback for subsequent actions. Model weights and the action interface remain fixed throughout. Across 12 real-world manipulation tasks, LEXP achieves $23/36$ successful trials (63.9\%), compared with $19/36$ (52.8\%) with memory alone and $2/36$ (5.6\%) for vanilla Astra. On three tasks, bread transfer, sort trash and toiletries, and retrieve drawer, removing planning reduces success from $7/9$ to $4/9$, while removing retained experience reduces it to $3/9$. Execution traces illustrate feedback-guided corrections and cross-episode reuse of an inspection strategy. Execution analyses illustrate how task structure and experience-derived feedback guide task progression, action correction, and experience reuse. These results support context-space adaptation as a practical mechanism for turning physical interaction into reusable guidance for robotic manipulation.

papers.title_en: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots
papers.authors: Xuanzhi Feng, Zeyu Liu, Weiheng Gao, Xinchen Li, Jiankun Tang, Fangqi Zhu, Quanxin Shou, Hao Chen, Zhengyang Yan, Hualei Zhang, Junhao Li, Zhiyao Wu, Jie Zhang, Song Guo
papers.evidence: 大模型智能体生成机器人控制程序并扩展技能库
papers.tldr: LLM机器人智能体虽能生成控制程序，但泛化到新任务常依赖复杂脚手架，仅扩充技能也难以评估新能力与识别边界。META-Robot将自我认知与能力扩展耦合，用动作级谓词显式化执行结果供LLM推理。智能体据此发现自身局限、扩展评价标准并结构化扩充技能，还引入本体感觉反馈锚定物理状态。仿真与真机实验显示任务表现、泛化、技能和评价标准持续扩展均提升。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based robotic agent systems can generate programs for robot control, yet their generalization to new tasks often depends on elaborate scaffolding. Expanding their skill repertoires alone offers limited guidance on how to assess new capabilities or identify what remains beyond their reach. We introduce META-Robot, a framework that couples self cognition with capability scaling by expanding the criteria through which an agent evaluates and develops its skills. At its core, action-level predicates make execution outcomes explicit and available for LLM reasoning. The agent uses these assessments to identify its own limitations, extend relevant evaluation criteria, and guide the structured expansion of its skills. Proprioceptive feedback further grounds this process in the robot's physical state, enriching the evidence available for self-cognition. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate stronger overall task performance, generalization to new tasks, continued expansion of skills and evaluation criteria, and effective use of non-visual proprioceptive signals.

papers.authors: Sombit Dey, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel
papers.evidence: 异步解耦高层VLM语义推理与低层动作生成
papers.tldr: 现有VLA将语义推理与动作执行串行在主控制环，模型规模增大带来延迟并损害实时反应。ARP用异步独立频率进程解耦二者：大VLM低频更新语义记忆，轻量视觉-动作专家基于该记忆高频输出动作。为应对记忆陈旧与执行延迟，训练专家时显式引入跨进程时间错配观测。Franka准静态任务成功率提升18%、执行时间减少20%，动态仿真达基线3-5倍，且VLM可降至1/10频率无明显损失。
papers.abstract_en: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a high-capacity Vision-Language Model (VLM) asynchronously updates a semantic memory at low fre- quency, while a lightweight Vision-Action Expert, conditioned on this semantic memory, generates robot actions at a much higher control frequency. Such a formulation, enables having a fast perception-action loop without compromising on the semantic capability. To overcome asynchronous memory staleness, ARP trains the vision-action expert on the semantic staleness and execution delay, with temporally mismatched observation across processes. On Franka manipulation tasks, ARP achieves an 18% higher success rate and 20% less time need for execution in quasi-static setups, while 3-5 times baseline performance in dynamic simulation environments. Furthermore, ARP enables operating the VLM at 10 times lower than its nominal frequency with no significant performance loss making it much more efficient than the baseline. These results highlight the architectural advantages of modeling robot policies as asynchronous processes, enabling real-world reactive deployment without sacrificing the scale of foundation models.

papers.title_en: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
papers.authors: Chao Liang, Ke Chen, Fengxiaoxiao Li, Shibo Huang, Yufeng Sun, Zhaokai Yin, Jianhuan Lai, Haozhe Feng, Chenghuan Jia, Zhipeng Zhang
papers.evidence: MetaBrain智能体提供运行时指导并调用VLA动作策略完成具身任务
papers.tldr: 针对机器人持续自主中的高效控制与故障恢复问题，作者提出以代码为扩展接口的具身多智能体框架A2-MEAS。该框架用修正代码融合语言、空间证据、执行历史与动作提议，并由MetaBrain提供训练监督和运行时指导。其动作模型A2-WLA引入运动感知历史与潜在世界模型，在BEHAVIOR、RoboTwin 2.0及真实机器人任务上取得显著提升。系统还实现高吞吐训练基础设施，并计划开源模型、脚本与系统，以支持高效具身学习研究。
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

papers.title_en: ReSkill: Selective Self-Improvement for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Zheng Sun, Zhihao Li, Zhuo Li, Wenrui Liu, Xin Wang, Fei Chen
papers.evidence: 编码智能体由指令与技能库构建任务图并修订技能
papers.tldr: 组合式机器人操作的自改进需决定复用、改进与保留哪些改动。ReSkill 让编码智能体从指令与技能库构建以对象为中心的任务图，用节点级执行记录定位失败，并在任务层与技能层做局部修订，经全任务评估和配对比较后采纳。在十项 RoboDojo 任务上，平均成功率由 30.0% 升至 86.2%，八项真实任务真机成功率为 77.5%，且中位修订仅改三个函数。该方法表明定位局部缺陷、验证候选改动并积累可复用技能，可提升组合式操作执行效果。
papers.abstract_en: Self-improvement on compositional manipulation tasks requires deciding what to reuse, where to improve, and which changes to retain. We present ReSkill, a selective self-improvement framework that concentrates revision on capability gaps. A coding agent constructs an object-centric task graph from an instruction and a skill library, then uses node-level execution records to locate failures. At the task level, it revises stage organization, hand-off conditions, and recovery routes; at the skill level, it strengthens perception, motion, manipulation, and verification capabilities that repeatedly fail. Candidate revisions undergo full-task evaluation and paired comparisons before adoption, allowing local changes to accumulate into validated skills and an independently executable policy. The agent participates only during development; the deployed policy calls the retained skills without invoking the agent at run time. On the same development set, average success across ten RoboDojo tasks rises from 30.0% for the initial versions to 86.2% for the final adopted programs; retained programs achieve 83.6% in recorded robustness and model-selection evaluations. Across eight real-world tasks, ReSkill succeeds in 72 of 80 rebuilt-simulation trials and 62 of 80 real-robot trials (77.5%). The median revision changes only three functions, approximately 0.5% of a program, while 39% of task-specific functions in later-added tasks directly reuse existing implementations. These results show how locating local deficiencies, validating candidate changes, and accumulating reusable skills can improve execution of compositional manipulation tasks.

papers.title_en: MATCH: Execution-Aware Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environment
papers.authors: Shuhao Ye, Yufei Wei, Demao Wang, Shichao Zhai, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang
papers.evidence: 语言条件规划器选择原语动作执行器的执行请求
papers.tldr: 连续环境视觉语言导航需在碰撞约束下兼顾指令规划与可靠执行，但现有分层方法多固定执行器、只优化规划器。MATCH 联合学习语言条件规划器与目标条件原子动作执行器，用执行感知拓扑图融合执行器价值与结果记忆，并通过有界连续偏移细化请求目标。仅 0.5B 参数即在 R2R-CE 和 RxR-CE 达到 SOTA，真实机器人初步部署也展示潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires instruction-consistent planning and reliable execution under collision constraints. Yet many hierarchical approaches optimize the planner while keeping execution fixed. We introduce MATCH, a framework that jointly learns a language-conditioned planner and a goal-conditioned primitive-action executor. An execution-aware topological graph represents start-dependent execution options and integrates executor value estimates with realized outcome memory, enabling the planner to select execution requests and refine their targets through bounded continuous offsets. A transition-aware dense macro reward balances ordered progress along the reference route against execution residual, encouraging executable requests without substituting local success for instruction following. A staged curriculum culminates in synchronized on-policy updates, with the executor learning on planner-generated requests and the planner adapting its requests to the executor's current behavior. With 0.5B parameters, MATCH achieves state-of-the-art performance on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks. Preliminary real-robot deployments further demonstrate its practical potential.

papers.title_en: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
papers.evidence: 用大模型将指令转为可供具身规划器执行的符号目标
papers.tldr: 具身智能体需将自然语言指令转成可执行符号目标，但生成与选择任一环节出错都会影响下游规划。本文提出两阶段“先生成后排序”方法：先监督微调LLM适配EAI输出约定，再用CORE从模型自身候选中学习完整输出偏好。在EAI家庭场景上，该方法优于简单提示、思维链和知识图谱基线，涵盖DeepSeek与Qwen等开源模型。这提升了符号目标解释的可靠性。
papers.abstract_en: Goal interpretation is to translate a natural language instruction into a formal symbolic goal that a planner can execute. It is critical for embodied agents because any error here propagates to every downstream planning and action step. Doing it well requires both generating suitable candidates and reliably selecting among them. We present a two-stage generate-then-rank approach to Goal Interpretation in the Embodied Agent Interface (EAI). First, supervised fine-tuning adapts a Large Language Model (LLM) to EAI's output convention. Second, Candidate-Output Ranking from Errors (CORE) learns preferences over complete outputs from the model's own generated alternatives. We conducted experiments on the household scenes of the Embodied Agent Interface Benchmark. Multiple open source LLMs including DeepSeek-V3 chat, DeepSeek-Reasoner, and Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-72B were evaluated. The proposed method outperformed the baseline models including LLMs with simple prompting, chain-of-thought, and knowledge graph based approaches.

papers.title_en: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation
papers.authors: Jiachen Tao, Gengyu Zhang, Haoxuan Wang, Bing Liu, Yan Yan
papers.evidence: 通过基元路由实现VLA技能保持与长程技能组合
papers.tldr: VLA部署需保留已学技能并在长程复合任务中按阶段调用，但共享更新缺乏可复用技能的参数位置与调用机制。PRISM把技能族存为低秩动作专家适配器组成原语库，加入技能专属残差，并用VLM条件的分块路由器在推理时组合。RoboCasa365上原子技能成功率56.43%、长程复合20.00%，优于π0.5-LoRA两阶段微调的17.86%与17.50%。这提供了可保留、可组合的VLA适配新路径。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models promise a single language-conditioned policy adaptable to many manipulation behaviors, yet deployment additionally requires skill retention and long-horizon composition: a policy must retain previously acquired skills and reuse them inside composite tasks whose behavior changes across phases. The standard recipe absorbs every new task into one shared update, which provides neither a parameter-level locus for reusable skills nor a mechanism for invoking each skill along the trajectory. We observe that this missing structure is latent rather than absent: per-skill low-rank updates of a pretrained VLA occupy a robustly distinguishable, low-dimensional subspace, and a single composite-task LoRA concentrates roughly half of its Frobenius energy in this subspace, against a near-zero matched random-rotation control. Building on this geometry, we introduce PRISM, which represents reusable skills as parameter-level primitives: each skill family is stored as a dedicated low-rank action-expert adapter in a primitive bank, primitives are augmented with skill-specific low-rank residuals and composed at inference by a per-chunk VLM-conditioned router that reads the prefix representation to track task progress, and the router is supervised by per-chunk labels from a deterministic, task-conditioned, action-derived oracle. During composite training, the vision encoder, the language LoRA, the skill residuals, the router, and the shared action projections and time MLP are updated; every primitive is held frozen, so the base per-skill action-expert adapters are preserved by construction. On RoboCasa365, PRISM achieves 56.43% atomic-skill success and reaches 20.00% on long-horizon composite tasks, while a standard $\pi_{0.5}$-LoRA two-stage fine-tune reaches 17.86% atomic and 17.50% composite success. We additionally validate PRISM on an AgileX PIPER real-robot setup.
